answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may post orders, with a delayed withdrawal period and slashing for provable double-spending or collusion. Splitting one budget across a ripple of fake identities does not create more buying power: every account ties up additional capital, and detected fraud forfeits it. The glacier-like delay also keeps attackers exposed after an attack, while a terrace of independent validators checks evidence before penalties land.
